name: Enquiry to signed client
description: From a new enquiry (website form, email or referral) to the onboarding call with a signed client, as Grace Adeyemi and Tom Whitfield describe it.

steps.name: Enquiry arrives
steps.notes: Three routes in (website form to the shared inbox, a direct email, a referral phone call); after the first look they all look the same.

steps.name: First look at enquiry
steps.notes: Grace looks at every enquiry herself: is it a real business, is there a budget. She replies usually before lunch, the next morning if she is out. No time given: "It's a coffee-length thing. I don't time it" (Grace, 00:03:55), and "No. Ask me something I can measure." (00:04:09).

assumed.hands_on_hours: Grace does not time it, but calls it "a coffee-length thing" (00:03:55) done as part of the morning, so a quarter of an hour. Assumed: a quarter of an hour (Austin said to assume).

steps.name: Wait for a diary slot
steps.notes: Calendar time between agreeing to talk and the call. Grace: sometimes next day if someone cancels, sometimes four days. Referrals get bumped to about next day, then the same as the rest (00:05:24).

wait_hours.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
wait_hours.quote: It's usually two or three days out before we can get them in.

assumed.wait_hours: Two to three days converted at a 7.5 hour working day (Austin: Copperleaf works a 37.5 hour week): 15 to 22.5 hours, 18.75 typical.

steps.name: Discovery call
steps.notes: Tom sits in on the big ones only. Grace does not record calls; she types notes. Only prospects who already spend on ads get an audit; Grace guessed "maybe a fifth" skip it (00:07:23), then said not to hold her to it and the interviewer left it out, so every enquiry is shown going through the audit.

steps.name: Audit ad accounts
steps.notes: Ellie mostly, Kofi if Ellie is slammed: account structure, spend, what is wasted. Grace first said "it varies a lot, depends whether it's a tidy account or a horror show" (00:07:55). Tom has "seen her do one in an afternoon and I've seen her at it for two days" (00:03:36).

wait_hours.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
wait_hours.quote: No, Ellie just picks it up the same day or the next, that's not a thing.

assumed.hands_on_hours: The interviewer proposed four hours ("So four hours for the audit?", 00:08:05) and Grace agreed with "Yeah, roughly." after saying it varies a lot; Tom has seen one take an afternoon and another two days. Austin confirmed four hours; Assumed (Austin said to assume).

steps.name: Pitch deck
steps.notes: Maddie Kerr does the deck; Grace gave no time for it ("I honestly couldn't tell you. She just gets it done.", 00:09:16). Grace briefs her the day before it is due. Tom looks at the deck before it goes out ("it's a glance", 00:04:26).

assumed.hands_on_hours: Nobody has timed it ("I honestly couldn't tell you. She just gets it done.", Grace, 00:09:16). Maddie is briefed the day before it is due (00:23:30), so it fits inside a day; Assumed: two hours (Austin said to assume).

steps.name: Write proposal
steps.notes: Queueing, not a fixed wait: proposals "sit on my desk a week because I'm pitching" (Grace, 00:11:29), "If I had two of me it'd be a day." (00:11:54). Promise to the client: "we promise a proposal within five working days of the call" (Grace, 00:12:41), counted from the call. Tom says a second version often needs his pricing again.

hands_on_hours.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
hands_on_hours.quote: The writing is the two, three hours.

hands_on_hours.speaker: Tom Whitfield
hands_on_hours.quote: it's a day and a half, all in.

rework_rate.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
rework_rate.quote: one proposal in four needs a second version.

waiting_now.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
waiting_now.quote: I've got five proposals on my desk at the moment.

sla_hours.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
sla_hours.quote: we promise a proposal within five working days of the call.

assumed.hands_on_hours: Grace's 2.5 h (two to three) is the writing alone; Tom's "day and a half" is working time, not elapsed (he confirmed at 00:05:30), 1.5 days at a 7.5 hour day (Austin: 37.5 hour week) = 11.25 h, and includes tailoring, scope back-and-forth with the client, chasing Maddie and sorting the numbers with him.
assumed.sla_hours: Five working days at a 7.5 hour day (Austin: 37.5 hour week) is 37.5 hours. The promise runs from the call, so it covers the audit, the deck and this step; it is kept here because this is the step that sends it.

steps.name: Pricing sign-off
steps.notes: Grace never mentions this step ("She thinks the proposal goes straight out. It doesn't.", Tom, 00:06:36). A strange one takes "an hour of me swearing at a spreadsheet" (00:07:06). Done in the gaps: "It's not a queue" (00:07:32). Separate from the day and a half of proposal work (00:19:35).

hands_on_hours.speaker: Tom Whitfield
hands_on_hours.quote: No, twenty. Twenty minutes, that's the honest one.

wait_hours.speaker: Tom Whitfield
wait_hours.quote: Not really. If it's in my inbox by lunch it's done by the end of the day.

steps.name: Client considers proposal
steps.notes: Grace chases around day ten. Proposals that go silent are called lost after a month, and silence is counted as lost ("We don't track it", 00:14:19). Tom: "That's about right. Some are quicker." (00:08:29).

assumed.wait_hours: Grace gave only a ceiling, "The client decision takes, well, within two weeks usually." (00:13:15), which is 10 working days at 7.5 h = 75 h, and "Some come back in a day" (7.5 h). The ceiling is used as the wait, with the range; confirm the typical wait.

steps.name: Send contract
steps.notes: From a template with the scope pasted in; Tom does it now, Grace used to. The three contracts counted are waiting on the client's signature, which "can take ages, it's up to them" (Grace, 00:15:27); Tom: "it can be a week, it can be the same day"; Harlow and Pike took three days but "Don't average that, it's one client." (00:12:02). Tom nudges people to sign, which is time inside this step.

wait_hours.speaker: Grace Adeyemi
wait_hours.quote: Tom does contracts now, more like two days.

waiting_now.speaker: Tom Whitfield
waiting_now.quote: Three contracts waiting on signatures right now.

assumed.wait_hours: Elapsed time from a yes to the contract going out, in working days at a 7.5 hour day (Austin: 37.5 hour week): Grace says two days (15 h), batched; Tom says a working day (7.5 h, confirmed at 00:11:26). Hands-on time to prepare one is not stated.

steps.name: Onboarding call
steps.notes: Tom plus whoever runs the account (Ellie or Kofi for paid media), so two people attend. Big accounts get a half-day workshop on top: "the big ones are a proper workshop, half a day, on top of the prep" (Tom, 00:13:39). Tom: the call is an hour, the reading up on the client, audit and proposal makes it two hours with prep, so the two figures count different things.
